operation.source_intent: Persist or update the exact onboarding site profile held by the flow, verify the real WordPress REST boundary, persist protected WordPress credentials only after successful verification, clear browser credential material, and then start the tenant-aware initial synchronization.

security.site_identity: server-owned active tenant context; caller-owned tenant_id, site_id, actor_user_id, status and other direct identifiers are rejected; after failed verification the server may issue an encrypted retry_token bound to operation + tenant + actor + failed site so only that server-selected profile can be retried
security.credential_storage: SiteCredential secret_value uses the encrypted cast and is written only after successful WordPress verification; failed verification stores no newly submitted credential and the secret is never returned
security.browser_secret_policy: Application Password state is cleared after submission and never echoed in rendered authoritative state
security.csrf: mutation is on the Laravel web/auth/tenant.context route stack and frontend apiRequest supplies the CSRF token
security.initial_sync_gate: SyncRun and SyncSiteJob are created/dispatched only after successful WordPress verification
security.idempotency: tenant-scoped Idempotency-Key receipts bind the request including server-resolved retry identity, reject conflicting reuse, and replay terminal outcomes; corrected retries use only a server-issued encrypted retry_token bound to operation + tenant + actor + failed site, never a caller-owned site id
security.audit: immutable tenant-scoped AuditEvent records credential persistence and verified queue/failure milestones without secrets
security.retry_token: opaque Laravel-encrypted retry token is returned only for failed verification, bound to operation + tenant + actor + site, validated server-side, and accepted only while that exact tenant-owned site remains failed
